references.record_title: Americans' Challenges with Health Care Costs
references.version_or_date: Published Oct 23, 2026; editorial note: updated October 23, 2026, originally published December 14, 2021
references.notes: Data note compiling several KFF polls. 44% from KFF Health Tracking Poll (May 5-26, 2025); 26% very worried from KFF Health Tracking Poll (September 16-21, 2026); 28% skipped care and 15%/27% health worse from KFF Survey of Health Access and Caregiving (May 4-26, 2026); 43%/19% from KFF Health Tracking Poll (Feb. 24 - Mar. 2, 2026); $500 bill from KFF Health Care Debt Survey (Feb. 25-Mar. 20, 2022). Prior '27% very worried' was the gasoline figure; corrected to 26%.

claims.text: 44% of adults say health care costs are difficult to afford
claims.quote: Just under half of U.S. adults say that it is very or somewhat difficult for them to afford their health care costs (44%).

claims.text: 26% are very worried about affording health care costs
claims.quote: about a quarter (26%) saying they are “very” worried about affording health care costs for themselves and their families

claims.text: 28% skipped or postponed needed care in the past 12 months because of cost
claims.quote: About three in ten (28%) adults say in the past 12 months they have skipped or postponed getting health care they needed because of the cost.

claims.text: 15% say health got worse after skipping or delaying care for any reason, including cost
claims.quote: about one in seven (15%) adults overall say their health got worse because they skipped or delayed needed care for any reason, including cost

claims.text: 27% among adults 18 to 64 with three or more health conditions
claims.quote: About one-third (36%) of adults ages 18-64 with three or more health conditions report ... and a quarter (27%) say their health got worse because they skipped or delayed care for any reason, including cost.

claims.text: 82% of uninsured vs 42% of insured adults under 65 find costs difficult to afford
claims.quote: Uninsured adults under age 65 are much more likely to say affording health care costs is difficult (82%) compared to those with health insurance coverage (42%).

claims.text: Three in ten insured adults under 65 skipped or postponed care because of cost
claims.quote: three in ten adults ages 18 to 64 with insurance still report not getting health care they needed due to cost.

claims.text: 43% did not take a medicine as prescribed because of cost, including 19% who cut pills or skipped doses (Feb to Mar 2026 poll)
claims.quote: About four in ten (43%) U.S. adults say they have not taken their medication as prescribed in the past year due to costs. This includes ... one in five (19%) who have cut pills in half or skipped doses

claims.text: About half could not pay an unexpected $500 medical bill, 19% not at all (2022 Health Care Debt Survey)
claims.quote: About half of U.S. adults say they would not be able to pay an unexpected medical bill that came to $500 out of pocket. This includes one in five (19%) who would not be able to pay it at all

claims.text: 88% of covered workers with single coverage have a general annual deductible
claims.quote: Eighty-eight percent of workers with single coverage have a general annual deductible that must be met before most services are paid for by the plan

claims.text: Average single-coverage deductible $1,886 among workers with a deductible (2025)
claims.quote: The average deductible amount in 2025 for workers with single coverage and a general annual deductible is $1,886, similar to last year.

claims.text: 34% have a single-coverage deductible of $2,000 or more, up 77% over ten years
claims.quote: Thirty-four percent of covered workers in 2025 are in a plan with a general annual deductible of $2,000 or more for single coverage ... has increased 32% over the last five years and 77% over the last ten

claims.text: Average premiums $9,325 single and $26,993 family in 2025
claims.quote: The average annual premiums for employer-sponsored health insurance in 2025 are $9,325 for single coverage and $26,993 for family coverage.

claims.text: Worker contributions $1,440 single and $6,850 family
claims.quote: The average annual contribution amounts for covered workers are $1,440 for single coverage, similar to the amount last year, and $6,850 for family coverage

references.version_or_date: Glossary page read 2026-11-15; lists plan years 2026 and 2027
references.notes: Figures are stated for Marketplace plans; page wording now says so.

claims.text: Out-of-pocket limit is the most you pay for covered services in a plan year; after it, the plan pays 100% of covered in-network benefits
claims.quote: The most you have to pay for covered services in a plan year. After you spend this amount on deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance for in-network care and services, your health plan pays 100% of the costs of covered benefits.

claims.text: 2026 Marketplace limit no more than $10,600 individual / $21,200 family
claims.quote: 2026: No more than $10,600 for an individual or $21,200 for a family

claims.text: 2027 limit $12,000 individual / $24,000 family
claims.quote: 2027: No more than $12,000 for an individual or $24,000 for a family

claims.text: Limit excludes premiums, out-of-network care and non-covered services
claims.quote: The out-of-pocket limit doesn't include: Your monthly premiums; Anything you spend for services your plan doesn't cover; Out-of-network care and services

references.record_title: Americans' Ability to Afford Healthcare Falls to Five-Year Low
references.notes: Press release from the index's co-publisher (West Health-Gallup Center on Healthcare in America).

claims.text: 49% Cost Secure, lowest since index began in 2021
claims.quote: fewer than half of Americans (49%) are considered “Cost Secure,” meaning they can consistently afford healthcare and prescription medications ... the lowest level recorded since West Health and Gallup launched its Healthcare Affordability Index in 2021.

claims.text: 41% Cost Insecure, 10% Cost Desperate (lacking access and unable to pay for both care and drugs)
claims.quote: Cost Insecure — lacking access to care or recently unable to pay for either care or medicine (41% of U.S. adults in 2025) ... Cost Desperate — lacking access and recently unable to pay for both care and prescription drugs

claims.text: Survey of 5,660 adults fielded October to December 2025
claims.quote: Results are based on a Gallup Panel study completed by 5,660 U.S. adults ages 18 and older, conducted Oct. 27-Dec. 22, 2025.

claims.text: 41% of adults currently had some debt caused by medical or dental bills (2022)
claims.quote: The KFF Health Care Debt Survey finds that 41% of adults currently have some debt caused by medical or dental bills.

claims.text: Among adults under 65, 44% of insured vs 62% of uninsured had current health care debt
claims.quote: among adults under 65, those who are currently uninsured are more likely to say they have health care debt than those who currently have health insurance (62% vs. 44%)

claims.text: 26% of adults in households earning $90,000 or more currently had health care debt
